# Sources: third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types.md
# (arrays and structs group recursively; neither is allowed in PARTITION BY)
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-schema-statements.md
# (graph element identity is its element table and key, not its properties).

# Nodes with identical visible properties still have distinct identities inside containers.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT [n] AS nodes, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.HiddenKeys MATCH (n:Person), (m:Person) RETURN n)
  GROUP BY nodes
)
=> "3"
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT STRUCT([STRUCT(n AS node)] AS nodes) AS s
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.HiddenKeys MATCH (n:Person), (m:Person) RETURN n)
)
=> "3"

# GQL grouping and WITH DISTINCT keep nested graph values across NEXT.
GRAPH scalar_graph.FinGraph
MATCH (n:Person), (m:Person)
RETURN [STRUCT(n AS node)] AS nodes, COUNT(*) AS c GROUP BY nodes
NEXT RETURN SUM(nodes[OFFSET(0)].node.id) AS result
=> "6"
GRAPH scalar_graph.HiddenKeys
MATCH (n:Person), (m:Person)
WITH DISTINCT STRUCT([n] AS nodes) AS s
RETURN COUNT(*) AS result
=> "3"

# Array order, length and empty arrays participate in grouping.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT [n, m] AS nodes
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.HiddenKeys MATCH (n:Person), (m:Person) RETURN n, m)
)
=> "9"
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT IF(k = 0, [], IF(k = 1, [n], [n, n])) AS nodes, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.HiddenKeys MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n), UNNEST([0, 1, 2]) AS k
  GROUP BY nodes
)
=> "7"

# Edge identity and composite node keys survive nested containers too.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT STRUCT(e AS edge) AS s
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.HiddenKeys MATCH ()-[e:Knows]->() RETURN e)
)
=> "4"
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT [STRUCT(n AS node)] AS nodes
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.CompoundGraph MATCH (n:Compound) RETURN n)
)
=> "3"

# NULL arrays, empty arrays and arrays containing NULL elements are distinct internal keys.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT IF(k = 0, NULL, IF(k = 1, [], [IF(FALSE, n, NULL)])) AS nodes, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.FinGraph MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n), UNNEST([0, 1, 2]) AS k
  GROUP BY nodes
)
=> "3"

# A NULL STRUCT differs from a non-NULL STRUCT whose graph field is NULL.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT IF(k = 0, NULL, STRUCT(IF(FALSE, n, NULL) AS node)) AS s, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.FinGraph MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n), UNNEST([0, 1]) AS k
  GROUP BY s
)
=> "2"

# Representatives retain properties, not just the identity used to group them.
SELECT SUM(nodes[OFFSET(0)].node.id) FROM (
  SELECT [STRUCT(n AS node)] AS nodes, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.FinGraph MATCH (n:Person), (m:Person) RETURN n)
  GROUP BY nodes
)
=> "6"

# Collation of scalar fields and identity of graph fields both apply to the same key.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT STRUCT(n AS node, COLLATE(v, 'und:ci') AS text) AS s, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.HiddenKeys MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n), UNNEST(['a', 'A']) AS v
  GROUP BY s
)
=> "3"

# INTERVAL fields still group by duration alongside graph identity.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT STRUCT(n AS node, i AS duration) AS s, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.HiddenKeys MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n),
    UNNEST([INTERVAL 1 YEAR, INTERVAL 12 MONTH]) AS i
  GROUP BY s
)
=> "3"
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT STRUCT(n AS node, i AS duration) AS s, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.HiddenKeys MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n),
    UNNEST([INTERVAL 1 YEAR, INTERVAL 12 MONTH]) AS i
  GROUP BY ROLLUP(s)
)
=> "4"

# Positional fields handle anonymous and duplicate STRUCT field names.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT STRUCT(n, n) AS s, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.HiddenKeys MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n)
  GROUP BY s
)
=> "3"
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT STRUCT(n AS node, m AS node) AS s, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.HiddenKeys MATCH (n:Person), (m:Person) RETURN n, m)
  GROUP BY s
)
=> "9"

# GROUPING SETS preserves the original containers and marks subtotal NULLs.
SELECT FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', COUNT(nodes), SUM(c), SUM(g)) FROM (
  SELECT nodes, COUNT(*) AS c, GROUPING(nodes) AS g
  FROM (SELECT [n] AS nodes FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.FinGraph MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n))
  GROUP BY ROLLUP(nodes)
)
=> "3:6:1"
SELECT SUM(nodes[OFFSET(0)].id) FROM (
  SELECT [n] AS nodes, COUNT(*) AS c
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.FinGraph MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n)
  GROUP BY ROLLUP(nodes)
)
=> "6"

# HAVING MAX with grouping sets uses the same recursive keys.
SELECT SUM(last.id) FROM (
  SELECT [n] AS nodes, ANY_VALUE(n HAVING MAX n.id) AS last
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.FinGraph MATCH (n:Person), (m:Person) RETURN n)
  GROUP BY ROLLUP(nodes)
)
=> "9"

# ARRAY and STRUCT partition keys stay rejected, including those with graph elements.
SELECT MAX(c) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.FinGraph MATCH (n:Person) RETURN COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY [n]) AS c)
=> error:
SELECT MAX(c) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.FinGraph MATCH (n:Person) RETURN COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY STRUCT(n AS node)) AS c)
=> error:
